text:
maya: heads-up — cluster gpu-pool-3 started hitting OOMs ~09:10 after the kernel-router merge that changed prefetch/kernsel ordering. not a whole outage but multiple nodes killed.

alon: ugh. which merge? link?

maya: https://phabricator/redwood/D9123 (kernel-router: prefer-prefetch before eviction). landed 09:02, rolled to pool-3 at 09:07.

rachel: saw a couple alerts in staging too. mem spike correlated with 4k+ seq requests.

samir: can you paste the OOM logs? quick grep?

maya: sure — snippet from node-17:

```
[2026-03-18T09:11:14Z] process[redwood-runtime]: killed by OOM, rss=87.2G, vms=94.1G, cmdline="runner --pool gpu-pool-3 --kernel=auto"
[2026-03-18T09:11:14Z] allocation backtrace: runtime::kv::prefetch() -> runtime::kv::reserve_for_prefetch() -> kernel_router::select_kernels()
```

samir: interesting, reserve_for_prefetch grabbed large contiguous heaplets and prevented later evict path from making progress.

alon: any CPU/pprof samples around spike? maybe kernel selection ended up choosing slower but hungry kernels on longctx.

maya: attached a quick heap profile from before/after. gist: https://gist.redwood/heap-288765

ci-bot: CI perf check failed on merge D9123: mem-usage regression +1.9x at seqlen=8192 (batch=1), alloc churn up 2.4x.

rachel: that's consistent. our autobatcher sends long sequences to prefer-prefetch path which keeps larger KV windows pinned.

samir: hypothesis: prefetch now tries to allocate full window up-front instead of incremental prefetch, triggering fragmentation under interleaved KV access patterns.

alon: can we reproduce locally with seqlen=8k and the new kernel-router? maya any repro cmd?

maya: yes — minimal repro run:

```
# reproduce (inside runtime-dev container)
./test_infer --model bertxlong --seq-len 8192 --batch 1 --workload long-prefixes --kernel-router=preft-first
```

maya: i ran that and saw OOM in ~120s, heap snapshots show many small slab fragments and a few giant reserved windows.

rachel: did you try toggling NEW_KERNEL_ROUTER=0 to force old behavior?

maya: yes — with KERN_ROUTER=legacy it runs fine. mem stable ~22G.

samir: bisect time. if D9123 is culprit, revert should fix. but let's bisect commits inside D9123; there were two sub-changes (prefetch sizing + kernel scoring tweak).

alon: i started a git bisect across the subcommits and pinned regression to 8b7d3f9 — the change that switches prefetch to allocate full window earlier (alloc-at-prefetch).

maya: 8b7d3f9 is the one.

ci-bot: bisect summary: culprit commit 8b7d3f9 (author: rla). Reproducer validated on 3 different hardware types (A100, H100L, V100-sim).

samir: ok. mitigation options:
- revert 8b7d3f9
- patch prefetch to return soft-reserve (no full commit) and fall back to incremental
- add a kernel-router override env to avoid alloc-at-prefetch for long sequences

maya: i've opened an emergency revert PR: https://phabricator/redwood/D9147 — rolling hold in progress.

deploy-bot: Rollout hold initiated for pool-3 and pool-4 by maya (reason: OOM regressions). Old binary pinned.

alon: before revert, can we test a conservative runtime flag to reduce prefetch aggressiveness? quick patch:

```
--kv-prefetch-max-bytes=16GB  # temp
--kv-prefetch-mode=incremental
```

rachel: that config reduced peak by ~30% in my local run but still higher than legacy. safe short-term if we pin.

samir: decision: revert commit 8b7d3f9 from the release branch, keep D9123 rolled back until we land an incremental prefetch implementation. also add a CI test for seqlen=8192 memory budget to catch regressions.

maya: filing follow-ups —
- D9147 revert PR
- D9152 feature-parity incremental prefetch (adds soft-reserve and graceful fallbacks)
- D9153 CI perf test: e2e mem budget seqlen=8192

maya: links: revert https://phabricator/redwood/D9147, prefetch-fix WIP https://phabricator/redwood/D9152

alon: add a canary with the new prefetch but with env override disabled; run against production traffic traces to validate fragmentation pattern.

rachel: also adding tracing to KV eviction to log if there are >8 partial windows pinned for a single request — helps guardrails.

samir: great. once revert lands i'll un-hold rollout and monitor.

maya: revert merged and rolled to pool-3 at 09:40. nodes stabilized, no further OOMs. recording post-mortem and follow-ups.

maya: postmortem notes: root cause = alloc-at-prefetch change that increased long-seq working set and created fragmentation, interacting badly with eviction heuristics under interleaved accesses. mitigations: revert, incremental prefetch design, CI seqlen memory guard, telemetry for pinned-window counts.

rachel: +1 for the CI guard. also let's add perf regression alert when mem growth >25% vs baseline for seqlen tests.

alon: thanks all — good catch. we'll pair on D9152 tomorrow.

samir: filing incident ticket INC-2026-0422 and tagging eng-runtime on the postmortem.

maya: thanks everyone :heart:
